text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT DETECTED — autoscale instability in us-west-2.
incident-bot: symptoms: sustained tokens/sec spike (~220k), queue_depth rising to ~420, and increased throttle_events. first page sent to oncall at 2026-03-15T02:12:01Z.

matt: saw the page, on it. verifying surface: are we seeing model-level throttles or infra queuing?

ashley: quick summary: frontend routing sent more traffic to g4 pools after a region failover 02:10. GPUs hit a hot shard which increased KV misses -> longer latencies -> queue backing. tokens/sec spike looks real (customer batch job).

leo: confirmed throttle_events spiked ~08:10 UTC too. logs: `throttle:{count:18, reason:"concurrency"}`. Looks like requests hit concurrency limits then queued.

matt: mitigation in progress: enabling burst capacity (pool-surge us-west-2) and temporarily bumping concurrency limit for model-llama-v2-13b on that pool. Doing a manual rollout to the canary set to drain backlog.

ashley: please also flip the fallback to the lighter quantized variant for non-critical routes: config snippet I'm pushing now:

```yaml
route_overrides:
  - route: "/api/v1/generate"
    fallback_model: "llama-v2-13b-q4"
    enable_fallback_on_capacity: true
    fallback_threshold_ms: 2500
```

anya: adding a dashboard tile for combined signal (tokens/sec, queue_depth, throttle_events). I'll put a heatmap and a 1m/5m series so we can see short spikes.

leo: for post-incident tuning proposal: current alerts are very chatty. we have: queue_depth > 100 (3m) -> page, tokens/sec > 80k (2m) -> page, throttle_events > 1 (1m) -> page. those thresholds are triggering on benign bursts.

ashley: agree — we should reduce noise. proposed changes:
- move queue_depth page threshold to 300 for 5m (alert still fires to #eng-sre as WARN at 150 for 3m)
- tokens/sec page threshold to 150k for 3m (lower-severity warning at 90k)
- throttle_events: switch to composite alert that pages only when throttle_events > 5 AND queue_depth > 200 within 2m.

anya: I can implement those in Datadog now. draft monitor queries:

```text
# Queue depth pager
avg(last_5m):avg:custom.redwood.queue_depth{region:us-west-2} > 300

# Tokens/sec pager
max(last_3m):sum:custom.redwood.tokens_per_sec{region:us-west-2} > 150000

# Composite throttle pager
( max(last_2m):sum:custom.redwood.throttle_events{region:us-west-2} > 5 ) && ( avg(last_2m):avg:custom.redwood.queue_depth{region:us-west-2} > 200 )
```

matt: +1 for debounce and composite. Also request adding a 10m auto-silence window for low-sev warn pages after an acknowledged incident to prevent duplicates.

infra-bot: NOTE: burst-capacity auto-up from pool-surge succeeded. pool metrics show queue_depth beginning to trend down.

leo: observed customer impact: 2 customers on high-qps plans reported 503s during 02:11-02:18 UTC. I'm logging impact for postmortem.

ashley: live mitigation summary: burst capacity + fallback routing + temporary concurrency bump. Backfill drained, latencies recovering.

anya: action items I'm taking now:
- create new Datadog monitors with the thresholds above
- add a composite monitor dashboard tile and a short-runbook blurb explaining when to flip canary vs burst
- add a 10m debounce on pages for these monitors and route WARN -> channel only

matt: I'll follow up with a short post-incident blameless writeup and propose a follow-up sync tomorrow 14:00 PT to review thresholds with product (esp. about allowing high tokens/sec batch jobs).

leo: also recommend a small synthetic test that ramps tokens/sec to 120k for 10m to verify autoscaler behavior before we lower any thresholds.

ashley: noted. set up a tracked ticket: SRE-4573 with checkboxes for monitor updates, dashboard, runbook, and the synthetic test. Please add any additional test cases.

anya: done — SRE-4573 created and assigned to me. I'll post the PR to monitors and the dashboard link here when ready.

matt: thanks all. reconvene in #eng-sre if anything reoccurs. marking this thread as acknowledged and moving to post-incident actions. :white_check_mark:
